The Dot Com bubble happened the same reason most crashes in recent history happened--The Fed was pumping massive amounts of reserves into the system, which got funneled into capital investment markets. And most of these went into Internet start-ups specifically because the Fed had also set interest rates artificially low, incentivizing far more investment and loan creation than was sustainable in the market. Tulipmania was something of a clusterfuck, but you can point to several cases of state intervention being responsible for it. Holland was debasing its own currency to fill its treasuries (essentially a precursor to the credit expansion practiced by the Fed and other central banks today).
